statement.text:
Let G(K) be the Chevalley group over a commutative ring K associated with
the root system Φ as defined in (R. Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley groups, Yale
Univ., New Haven, Conn., 1967). This group is generated by the root subgroups
xr (K), r ∈ Φ. We define an elementary carpet of type Φ over K to be any collection
of additive subgroups {Ar | r ∈ Φ} of K satisfying the condition
             cij,rs Air Ajs ⊆ Air+js       for r, s, ir + js ∈ Φ, i > 0, j > 0,
where cij,rs are constants defined by the Chevalley commutator formula and Air =
{ai | a ∈ Ar }. What are necessary and sufficient conditions (in terms of the Ar ) on
the elementary carpet to ensure that the subgroup ⟨xr (Ar ) | r ∈ Φ⟩ of G(K) intersects
with xr (K) in xr (Ar )? See also 15.46.                                 V. M. Levchuk
